summary: This note is an overview of the United States men's national soccer team, which is controlled by the United States Soccer Federation and competes in CONCACAF. It covers the team's World Cup history, from its 1930 semi-final finish and 1950 win over England to its seven straight appearances from 1990 to 2014 and its failure to qualify for 2018. It also summarizes the team's results in the CONCACAF Gold Cup and Copa América and notes that the head coaching job is vacant after Bruce Arena resigned, with Dave Sarachan as interim coach.
one_line: Overview of the U.S. men's national soccer team's World Cup, continental tournament, and coaching history.
key_facts: The United States men's national soccer team is controlled by the United States Soccer Federation.
The team competes in the Confederation of North, Central American and Caribbean Association Football (CONCACAF).
The team has appeared in ten FIFA World Cups, including the first in 1930, where it reached the semi-finals.
The U.S. won 1-0 against England at the 1950 World Cup.
After 1950, the U.S. did not qualify for the World Cup until 1990.
The U.S. hosted the 1994 World Cup, where it lost to Brazil in the round of sixteen.
The U.S. qualified for five more consecutive World Cups after 1990, for a total of seven straight appearances, a feat shared with only seven other nations.
The U.S. reached the quarter-finals of the 2002 World Cup, where it lost to Germany.
In the 2009 Confederations Cup, the U.S. eliminated top-ranked Spain in the semi-finals before losing to Brazil in the final, its only appearance in a final.
The team failed to qualify for the 2018 World Cup after being eliminated in continental qualifying, ending its streak of consecutive World Cups at seven.
The U.S. has hosted fourteen editions of the CONCACAF Gold Cup, winning six.
The U.S. has achieved a fourth-place finish in two Copa Américas, including the 2016 edition that it hosted.
The team's head coaching position is currently vacant, as most recent coach Bruce Arena resigned in October 2017.
Dave Sarachan is the team's interim head coach.
